extracted.intended_audience: DHS adjudicators, immigration attorneys, applicants, and stakeholder commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural guidance governing how DHS will determine whether a noncitizen is "likely at any time to become a public charge," including which benefits are considered/excluded, required factors (including the Affidavit of Support), officer procedures, and efforts to mitigate chilling effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Totality of the circumstances assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The public charge inadmissibility determination is a prospective determination made in the totality of the noncitizen's circumstances 'in the opinion' of the immigration officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will issue sub-regulatory guidance to identify a range of nonbinding considerations and to update them as data and circumstances evolve. The totality approach provides clarity and predictability and is intended to be administered consistently with statutory text and longstanding case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective, data-informed consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: When DHS issues guidance to officers that informs the totality of the circumstances assessment, such guidance will consider how these factors affect the likelihood that a noncitizen will become a public charge at any time, and will be based on an empirical analysis of the best-available data as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The data-informed considerations are meant to be nonbinding, updated as better data become available, and used to inform but not supplant individualized officer judgments; DHS acknowledges it cannot eliminate possible officer bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: primary dependence for subsistence
rubrics_metrics.description: A noncitizen is a 'public charge' if they are likely at any time to become primarily dependent on the government for subsistence, as demonstrated by either the receipt of public cash assistance for income maintenance or long-term institutionalization at government expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition focuses on the individual's degree of dependence on government support rather than the overall scale of government expenditures for particular programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of past or current receipt of specified public benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will consider the past or current receipt of public cash assistance for income maintenance and long-term institutionalization at government expense when making public charge inadmissibility determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officers will take into account amount, duration, and recency of such receipt; however, past or current receipt of public benefits is not alone dispositive of inadmissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount, duration, and recency of benefit receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: When benefit receipt is considered, officers should evaluate the amount, the duration, and the recency of the applicant's receipt of public cash assistance or long-term institutionalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements inform whether benefit receipt indicates primary dependence; more recent, larger, or longer-duration receipt is more probative of future primary dependence.

rubrics_metrics.name: No single factor should be dispositive (except limited exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public charge inadmissibility determinations must be based on the totality of the individual's circumstances and no one factor, other than the lack of a sufficient Affidavit of Support Under Section 213A of the INA (if required), should be the sole criterion for determining an applicant is likely at any time to become a public charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule bars treating any single element (e.g., benefit receipt, health condition) as automatically conclusive; adjudicators must weigh multiple factors together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Support (Section 213A) sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an Affidavit of Support Under Section 213A of the INA is required, the sufficiency of that affidavit bears on the public charge determination; lack of a sufficient affidavit, if required, renders a noncitizen inadmissible under the public charge ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit's sufficiency is the one factor that may by itself render an applicant inadmissible; determination of affidavit sufficiency is distinct from and separate in timing from the public charge prediction, and enforcement of the affidavit's obligations occurs after admission or adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit determinations to specified statutory factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Public charge inadmissibility determinations will be limited to the specified statutory factors; the Affidavit of Support Under Section 213A where required; and current and/or past receipt of TANF; SSI; State, Tribal, territorial, or local cash benefit programs for income maintenance and long-term institutionalization at government expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will not expand the universe of factors beyond those specified by statute and rule; officers should rely on the enumerated statutory factors when conducting determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of supplemental and special-purpose benefits (e.g., SNAP, housing)
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will not consider special purpose and supplemental programs such as SNAP and affordable housing programs in public charge inadmissibility determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: such programs are less probative of primary dependence (they are supplemental, modest, and often support work), their consideration would add little value while potentially causing chilling effects among eligible individuals; USDA and other agencies' input supports SNAP's supplemental nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider family status and household size, without stereotyping
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will consider family status and household size consistent with the rule's standards in determining likelihood of becoming a public charge, but will not rely on generalizations about the relative size of immigrant households.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officers should evaluate household composition as one factor in the totality of circumstances, avoiding unsupported generalizations about immigrant families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider education and skills (limited scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule includes the applicant's education and skills among factors considered when assessing likelihood of becoming a public charge, but DHS will not analyze an applicant's 'utility' to the U.S. labor market nor assess broader economic impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education and skills are relevant to an applicant's ability to be self-sufficient under the totality analysis, but officers must avoid using these attributes to measure general economic contributions or market effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation of chilling effects
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS recognizes and has considered historical 'chilling effects' of public charge policies and seeks to reduce unwarranted deterrence from benefit enrollment among people who are not subject to the public charge ground of inadmissibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS weighed previous guidance, judicial opinions, evidence of disenrollment after earlier rules, and public comments; the rule is designed to avoid causing eligible individuals to forgo benefits and is not to be evaluated by disenrollment among populations not subject to the ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officer procedures: articulation and opportunity to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS adjudicators are trained professionals; adjudicators will specifically articulate the reasons for a proposed adverse determination and will provide an opportunity for the applicant to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural safeguard is intended to improve fairness and reduce arbitrary outcomes; DHS acknowledges it cannot eliminate bias but must document reasons for adverse findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of application (who is covered)
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule applies to noncitizens applying for admission or adjustment of status and does not apply to nonimmigrants seeking extension of stay or change of status in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule is therefore limited in scope compared to some past rules; the included table on benefit eligibility is for background only and should not be used to determine benefits eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation focused on dependence, not government expenditure
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS interprets 'public charge' by reference to the degree of an individual's dependence on the government for support, rather than the scale of overall government expenditures for particular programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps focus determinations on applicants likely to rely primarily on government subsistence rather than measuring aggregate program costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural change: integrate public charge questions into Form I-485
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will not require a separate information-collection form regarding the public charge ground of inadmissibility but will incorporate a more manageable set of questions in Form I-485, Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces paperwork burden on applicants compared to prior approaches that used a separate form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with statutory text, Congressional intent, and case law
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule is promulgated to be consistent with the statutory text of section 212(a)(4) of the INA (8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4)) and the statement of national policy in 8 U.S.C. 1601, and to mirror longstanding case law and prior administrative practice where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS considered legislative history, PRWORA effects, the 1999 Interim Field Guidance, and the 2019 Final Rule when crafting the final rule; portions of prior guidance are adopted only where analyzed and appropriate rather than wholesale.
